Smt. Neetu Devi And Ors. vs The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
Thru. ... on 12 May, 2023

Author: Jaspreet Singh
Bench: Jaspreet Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc-Lko:33624
Court No. - 19
Case :- First Appeal From Order

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: No. - 605 of 2019 Appellant :- Smt. Neetu Devi And Ors.
Respondent :- The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Thru. B.M. And Ors.
Counsel for Appellant :- Amit Tripathi,Rashmi Rajvanshi Counsel for Respondent :- Vaibhav Raj Hon'ble Jaspreet Singh,J.
1. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants and Shri Vaibhav Raj, learned counsel for the respondent no.1.
None has put in appearance on behalf of the respondents no.2 and 3.

Accordingly,
the Court has proceeded to hear the matter on merits in absence of the respondents no.2 and 3 who are the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

2. The instant appeal has been preferred under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act by the claimants seeking enhancement in the award dated 28.08.2019 passed by the Motor Accident Claim Petition/District Judge, Faizabad in Claim Petition No.5 of 2017 whereby on the death of Sanjai Kumar a sum of Rs.4,20,000/- alongwith 6% interest has been awarded in favour of the claimants-appellants.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition/District Judge, Faizabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Submission of the learned counsel for the appellants is that the deceased Sanjai Kumar was a skilled labour engaged in the vocation of affixing tiles.

A clear statement was made by the wife of the Smt. Neetu Devi And Ors. vs The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Thru. ... on 12 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100034933/
1 deceased that her husband was engaged in the said vocation and was earning a sum of Rs.9000/-
per month.

entities.text: Smt. Neetu Devi And Ors. vs The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Thru
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
4. It is urged that the Tribunal has not appreciated the aforesaid aspect on the ground that since no documentary evidence was filed to establish the income of the deceased, accordingly taking a notional income of Rs.3000/- per month, the award has been calculated on the aforesaid basis.
5.

It is urged that since the accident took place in the year 2016 as per the rates prevailing for unskilled labour the Tribunal ought to have minimum taken a sum of Rs.200 per day as the base for calculating the income which has not been done.
6. It is also urged that the future prospects of the deceased has not been taken especially when he was 38 years of age.

It is also submitted that the amount awarded under the non conventional head is also extremely meager and is not in consonance with the decision rendered by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC page 680 as well as Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram 2018 SCC OnLine SC 1546.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC page 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram 2018 SCC OnLine SC 1546
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For the aforesaid reasons, it is urged that the award needs to be enhanced.

7. Shri Vaibhav Raj learned counsel for the respondent no.1 refuting the aforesaid submissions has stated that it was the primary duty of the claimants/appellants to have established the income of the deceased.

There is no clear statement nor any document brought on record to establish the income of the deceased and considering the fact and the circumstances a sum of Rs.3000/- per month has been taken as the notional income which cannot be said to be incorrect or on the lower side.

8. It is also urged that for the aforesaid reasons where the claimants could not establish the income of the deceased the question of future prospects was addressed by the Tribunal but it has been declined and the same also does not require any interference from this Court, accordingly the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
9. The Court has heard the learned counsel for the parties and also perused the material on record.
10. The only issue which is for consideration of this Court is whether the Tribunal has awarded a just and fair compensation in the facts and circumstances.

11. Since there is no challenge from the side of the respondents either by filing separate appeal or any cross appeal thus the findings returned by the Tribunal on the issue of the factum of the accident, the involvement of the vehicle, the offending vehicle being duly insured and the driver having a valid and subsisting license which have been returned by the Tribunal are accepted by the Court.

12. Having regard to the issue which has been raised by the learned counsel for the parties, the undisputed facts are that a deceased was aged about 38 years and is survived by his mother, wife and four children.

The record would indicate that the claimant witness no.1 Smt. Neetu who is wife of the deceased has entered into the witness box and gave a clear statement that her husband was Smt. Neetu Devi And Ors. vs The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Thru. ... on 12 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100034933/
2 engaged in affixing tiles and used to work with great proficiency and was able to earn about Rs.9000/- per month.

entities.text: Smt. Neetu Devi And Ors. vs The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Thru
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This witness was also cross

- examined by the respondents and even in her cross examination, she reiterated her stand that the deceased was engaged in the vocation of affixing tiles though she did not know where he worked but as and where and when the work was available he used to go and discharge his duties and functions.
13.

From the perusal of the aforesaid statement, it would be clear that in so far as the factum regarding the involvement of the deceased in the vocation of affixing tiles is concerned, there is no discrepancy and the said statement has remain steadfast in the examination-in-chief as well as in the cross examination.
However, the Tribunal has taken the notional income of Rs.3000/- per month only on the ground that there is no documentary evidence to support the fact.
14. Be that as it may, the mere fact that there is no documentary evidence would not mean that there is no income of the deceased.

In light of the statement which has been made and noticed as well as in absence of any contradictory material or evidence on record to establish that the deceased was not at all engaged in the vocation of affixing tiles, it cannot be said that he was absolutely worthless or was not involved in any vocation.

Thus, taking note of the aforesaid and in absence of any documentary evidence considering the fact that the accident took place in the year 2016, appropriate notional income ought to have been rupees six thousand per month.

15. It is also to be noticed that the Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra) having taken note of the issue of future prospects also in relation to such cases where the income was not established as held as under:-

"Though it may seem appropriate that there cannot be certainty in addition of future prospects to the existing income unlike in the case of a person having a permanent job, yet the said perception does not really deserve acceptance.

We are inclined to think that there can be some degree of difference as regards the percentage that is meant for or applied to in respect of the legal representatives who claim on behalf of the deceased who had a permanent job than a person who is self-employed or on a fixed salary.
But not to apply the principle of standardization on the foundation of perceived lack of certainty would tantamount to remaining oblivious to the marrows of ground reality.
And, therefore, degree-test is imperative.
Unless the degree-test is applied and left to the parties to adduce evidence to establish, it would be unfair and inequitable.
The degree-test has to have the inbuilt concept of percentage.

Taking into consideration the cumulative factors, namely, passage of time, the changing society, escalation of price, the change in price index, the human attitude to follow a particular pattern of life, etc., an addition of 40% of the established income of the deceased towards future prospects and where the deceased was below 40 years an addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years would be reasonable.
The controversy does not end here.
The question still remains whether there should be no addition where the age of the deceased is more than 50 years.
Sarla Verma Smt. Neetu Devi And Ors. vs The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Thru.

entities.text: Sarla Verma Smt. Neetu Devi And Ors. vs The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Thru
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
... on 12 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100034933/
3 thinks it appropriate not to add any amount and the same has been approved in Reshma Kumari.
Judicial notice can be taken of the fact that salary does not remain the same.
When a person is in a permanent job, there is always an enhancement due to one reason or the other.
To lay down as a thumb rule that there will be no addition after 50 years will be an unacceptable concept.
We are disposed to think, there should be an addition of 15% if the deceased is between the age of 50 to 60 years and there should be no addition thereafter.
Similarly, in case of self- employed or person on fixed salary, the addition should be 10% between the age of 50 to 60 years.

The aforesaid yardstick has been fixed so that there can be consistency in the approach by the tribunals and the courts."
--------******-------*******-------*****---------*** 59.4.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

16. In view of the aforesaid, the claimants would also be entitled to the future prospects which are applicable in the instant case as per the dictum of the Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra).
17. Now the issue regarding the grant of compensation under the non conventional heads are concerned, it would be seen that the deceased is survived by his four children, mother and his wife.
Each of the aforesaid persons are entitled to consortium in terms of their loss.

Accordingly, the four children would be entitled to parental consortium whereas the mother would be entitled to filial consortium and the wife would be entitled to spouse consortium (see Magma General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs Nanu Ram (supra).

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs Nanu Ram
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering that the amount of loss of estate and funeral expenses which has been granted by the Tribunal is at the rate of rupees five thousand which is also quite meager.

Noticing the fact that even in the decision of the Apex Court Pranay Sethi (supra)
which was noticed that such rates were to be enhanced at the rate of ten per cent every three years.
Hence, taking note of the aforesaid and applying it to the present case and the circumstances,, this Court re-determines the compensation
as under:-

Income = Rs.6000/- per month   Add:- 40% towards future prospects:- =Rs.24,00/- 
 Total Income = Rs.8400/- 
 Less:- (1/4th ) = Rs.2100/- 
 (deduction for 6 number of dependents  on personal expenses) 
 Thus total income = Rs.6300/- per month Smt. Neetu Devi And Ors. vs The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Thru. ... on 12 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100034933/
4  Age = 38 years  Multiplier = 15  Thus compensation payable = 6300x12x15=11,34,000/-
 Add:- Spouse consortium = Rs.40,000/-
Parental consortium (four children) = Rs.40,000/-

Filial consortium for parents = Rs.40,000/-
 Loss of estate = Rs.15000/-
Accordingly, the Court is of the view that the claimants are entitled to compensation as determined above alongwith interest at the rate six per cent per annum.
Any amount already paid to the claimants shall be deducted from the aforesaid amount.
The remaining shall be paid by the respondents to the claimants within a period of 60 days from the date a copy of this order is placed before the Authority concerned.
19. The appeal stands allowed in the aforesaid terms.
There shall be no order as to costs.
The record of the Tribunal be returned expeditiously.

(Jaspreet Singh, J.) Order Date :- May 12th, 2023 ank/-
